battle.name: 隋統一戰爭
battle.theater: 長江中下游：永安、采石至建康
battle.brief: 開皇元年（581）十一月楊堅受周恭帝禪稱帝，到開皇九年（589）二月隋軍入建康、陳朝覆亡，這是一場歷時八年的體系性戰爭。卡面羅馬方陣盾並未隨軍南下，它標示的是以盾結陣抵禦投射物的技術譜系；隋軍真正靠的是弩、槊、覆布車與五牙大艦。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 隋統一戰爭不是兩國對壘的一場會戰，而是從開皇元年到開皇九年、由北向南推進的一整套體系性戰爭，交戰方的名字也不止兩個。北方的開國一方是隋朝：楊堅以關隴集團接替北周，先在開皇元年前後平掉鄴城、蜀地與江南的殘餘勢力，再把軍權收攏到宿衛與新整的府兵手上，關中、洛陽的倉儲與開皇四年新開的永濟渠構成這支部大軍的補給骨架。軍隊編成分舟師、步騎、攻城部隊與力役四類：舟師統轄戰船與糧船，步騎分列各道，攻城部隊攜帶弩、發石車、撞車與雲梯，力役負責造船、修渠與轉運。南方的受攻一方是南朝末代的陳朝，都建康，領江淮以南與嶺南：樞密院掌軍籍與調發，鎮東大將軍蕭摩訶守京口，荊州刺史淳于量、徐州刺史裴忌各領州郡兵，江防舟師與建康禁軍是陳朝最後的依賴，州郡徵發兵則散在長江沿線一線。第三條戰線在北方邊境：漠北突厥聯盟自開皇元年沙摩羅弒佗斤而內亂不休，隋朝一面扶持內屬可汗分化汗庭，一面以白道之役打疼南犯的騎兵；東北的高句麗與西北的吐谷渾則各自分走隋軍的注意力，讓陳朝始終等不到北方援助。三條戰線彼此交錯，這就決定了這場戰爭的整體形態：它是一場以工程、糧秣與時間換取決定的持久戰。
countriesEn: The Sui unification war was not a single engagement between two armies ranged against each other; it was a whole systematic war driven from north to south between the first year of Kaihuang and the ninth, and the names of the belligerents run to more than two. On the northern side was the founding state, the Sui: Yang Jian took over from Northern Zhou with the Guanzhong and Longxi group behind him, first disposing of the surviving powers at Ye, in Shu and in Jiangnan around the first year of Kaihuang, and then concentrating military authority in the palace guards and in the reformed fubing, while the depots of Guanzhong and Luoyang and the Yongji canal newly cut in Kaihuang 4 formed the supply backbone of the great army. The troops were divided into four kinds: river fleets, infantry and cavalry, siege troops and labour. The fleets had the warships and the grain boats; infantry and cavalry were posted along the several lines of advance; the siege troops carried crossbows, stone-throwers, rams and scaling ladders; and the labour corps built the ships, worked the canals and moved the transport. On the side that was attacked stood the last southern dynasty, the Chen, with its capital at Jiankang and its territory south of the Huai and the Yangtze and through Lingnan: the Directorate of Military Affairs held the registers of soldiers and the dispatch of troops, the General of the Eastern Army Xiao Mohe held Jingkou, the Inspector of Jingzhou Chunyu Liang and the Inspector of Xu Pei Ji each commanded the levies of their commanderies, and the river fleet and the palace guard of Jiankang were the last supports on which the Chen relied, while the conscripted county troops lay strung out along the river. A third line of war ran along the northern frontier. In the steppe the Turkic confederation was tearing itself apart from Kaihuang 1, when Shamoro killed the child Qaghan Tuojin; the Sui at once propped up the pro-Sui qaghans in order to split the court, and beat the invading horsemen at the battle of White Way. In the northeast Goguryeo and in the northwest the Tuyuhun each drew away part of the Sui attention, so that the Chen could never expect help from the north. The interlocking of these three lines decided the shape of the war as a whole: it was a long war in which decisions were bought with engineering, with grain and with time.
people: 做決定的人分在兩邊。隋文帝楊堅是全場最高的決策者：他以大丞相與隋王的身份在開皇元年十一月受周恭帝禪，建立隋朝，此後二十年裡他做的最要緊的一件事，就是把南北分立的格局一次解決；開皇七年第一次伐陳在洞口大敗之後，他沒有急著再攻，而是用五年時間把舟師、糧秣與運河整備好，開皇八年十月才下達全面伐陳的詔令。開皇九年出兵時，實際在江上指揮的是晉王楊廣，他以行軍元帥與淮南行省尚書令的身份總攬東線，坐鎮廣陵，造舟、徵糧、操練水軍；上游主帥是司空楊素，他督造五牙大艦與黃龍艦，率眾自永安順流而下，過三峽時縱火破陳的阻截；秦王楊俊在襄漢一線策應，元帥副將王誼自襄陽、荊州方向南下，在湖北擊破淳于量。兩支奇兵是韓擒虎與賀若弼：韓擒虎以五百精兵夜渡采石，賀若弼在廣陵預造商船六十餘艘，夜裡換人為隋軍士卒，順流取采石，兩人出發前已約定同時發動。北方另有高熲以三十萬眾出師攻高句麗，賀婓子干率軍擊吐谷渾，替正面戰線分走壓力。陳朝一端留下姓名的，是陳帝叔寶與張麗華、孔貴嬪，能打仗的是鎮東大將軍蕭摩訶，掌樞密的是蔡大寶，陳帝最倚重的近臣施文慶屢次勸遷都以為不可行。隋廷內部反對出兵者亦有聲音，蘇威力諫開皇九年不可再伐，文帝幾乎要加害，終究未聽。
peopleEn: Those who took the decisions fall into two camps. Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, was the highest decision-maker in the whole affair: having taken the abdication of the Zhou child-emperor in the eleventh month of Kaihuang 1 in the capacity of grand chancellor and Prince of Sui, he founded the dynasty, and the single most important thing he did in the twenty years that followed was to settle the long division of north and south in a single stroke. After the first campaign against Chen was beaten at Dongkou in Kaihuang 7, he did not attack again in a hurry; he spent five years bringing the river fleet, the grain and the canals into order, and only in the tenth month of Kaihuang 8 did he issue the edict for the general campaign against Chen. When the army went out in Kaihuang 9, the man actually directing things on the river was the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, who as supreme commander and director of the Hongnan region took charge of the eastern line, sat at Guangling, and saw to the building of ships, the levying of grain and the training of the river troops. The commander on the upper river was the chancellor Yang Su, who supervised the construction of the great five-toothed ships and the yellow dragon ships, led the host down from Yong'an with the current, and broke the Chen obstruction in the gorges with fire. The Prince of Qin, Yang Jun, operated on the Xiangyang-Han line, and the deputy supreme commander Wang Yi came down from the Xiangyang and Jingzhou direction and defeated Chunyu Liang in Hubei. The two shock troops were Han Qinhu and He Ruobi: Han Qinhu crossed at Caishi in the night with five hundred picked men, and He Ruobi had sixty-odd merchant ships built in secret at Guangling, and at night the cargo was struck out and Sui soldiers put in, so that the fleet drifted down to take Caishi; the two had agreed before setting out to strike at the same moment. On the northern front Gao Jiong went out against Goguryeo with three hundred thousand men, and He Lou Ziggan led a force against the Tuyuhun, taking pressure off the main line. On the Chen side the names that survive are that of the emperor Chen Shubao, of Zhang Lihua and of the Lady Kong, the one commander who could really fight being the General of the Eastern Army Xiao Mohe, while the director of the secretariat was Cai Dabao; the courtier the emperor relied on most, Shi Wenqing, argued again and again for moving the capital and was told each time that it could not be done. There were voices in the Sui court against the campaign as well: Su Wei pressed the emperor in Kaihuang 9 not to attack again, and the emperor came close to doing him harm, but in the end did not listen.
kits: 卡面那面羅馬方陣盾並沒有隨隋軍南下，這一點必須先說清楚。Scutum 是公元前最後一個世紀羅馬軍團的制式裝備：凸面的長方盾，高約一百零五公分，寬約八十公分，木胎蒙皮，鑲金屬包邊，全重約六七公斤，盾緣做得平直而微彎，正是為了讓相鄰的盾牌彼此扣住、連成一堵可以移動的牆；羅馬人用它在野戰中擋住投射物，在攻城時拼成龜甲陣，護著撞槌與攻城塔推進。放到隋代的裝備表裡，同一位置上的東西是南北朝以來的那一套：步兵用木胎蒙皮或髹漆的虎頭牌、燕尾牌與步槊牌，牌面飾獸首，攜帶的作用是遮蔽而不是咬合；隋軍帳下還備有櫓盾、拒馬槊與鹿角拒馬，陳軍則用木製的櫓盾和長槊抵禦登岸的衝鋒。真正決定江面與城下勝負的是另一批裝備：遠射靠蹶張弩，木臂金屬機括，以足踏張弦，一發一矢，射程可及二百步上下，弓則輔之；重裝步兵著明光甲、戴兜鍪，執長槊白刃，騎兵成縱隊；攻城用發石車、撞車、雲梯、巢車與覆布車，覆布車蒙布與牛皮，推到城下，人在車上射擊、縱火，以減矢石之害；舟師有五牙大艦，艦身高十餘丈、上起層樓、可容數百人，另有黃龍、黃鶴諸艦與拍竿，專用來撞碎陳軍連綴的戰船。火是開皇八年之後的關鍵器材：火炬、油瓶、薪柴之外，隋船備帷幕與水桶，遇陳人投來火炬便以帷幕遮蔽、灑水滅火，冒著矢石突陣，砍斷陳軍的連鎖。糧秣與運輸靠牛馬挽車、運糧船隊與運河，士卒自負三日口糧。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card did not march south with the Sui army, and that has to be said first. The scutum was the regulation shield of the Roman legion in the last century BC: a convex rectangle about one hundred and five centimetres high and eighty wide, a wooden core covered in hide, edged with metal, weighing some six to seven kilograms, with the rim left flat and slightly turned so that neighbouring shields would lock into one another and form a wall that could move. The Romans used it to stop missiles in the open field, and in sieges they closed it into the testudo to cover the ram and the siege tower as they advanced. Set into the equipment table of the Sui, the things standing in the same place are the set that had come down since the Southern and Northern Dynasties: infantry carried the tiger-head, swallow-tail and spear-boards of wood covered in hide or lacquer, with animal heads on the face, and their function was to cover a man rather than to lock with his neighbour. The Sui camp also had wooden tower shields, boar-spear pickets and antler-shaped obstacles, while the Chen used wooden tower shields and long spears to hold off the assault as it came ashore. What really decided the river and the foot of the wall was another set of things. Long range work was done by the drawn crossbow, with a wooden stock and a metal lock, the string spanned by foot, one bolt to a shot, effective to something like two hundred paces, with the bow as its secondary. Armoured infantry wore bright plate and carried helmets and held the long spear in white steel, and cavalry moved in columns. For sieges there were the stone-thrower, the ram, the scaling ladder, the nest-tower and the cloth-covered vehicle, the last covered with cloth and hide and pushed up to the wall so that the men aboard could shoot and set fire and so take less harm from arrows and stones. The river fleet had the great five-toothed ship, more than ten zhang high, with tiered galleries on it and room for several hundred men, together with the yellow dragon and yellow crane ships and their polearms, built to smash the Chen vessels lashed together side by side. Fire was the critical material after Kaihuang 8: torches, jars of oil and firewood, and on top of that the Sui ships carried screens and buckets, and when the Chen threw torches they covered themselves with the screens and doused the fire, charged forward under arrows and stones and cut the Chen lashings apart. Grain and transport rested on oxen and horses pulling carts, on grain fleets and on the canals, with each soldier carrying three days' rations on his own person.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以用一句話概括：把戰爭做成工程，再用工程去換決定。第一步是開皇七年的敗績。隋軍初渡長江，在峽中被陳將蕭摩訶以火攻燒船，士卒死者十居七八，敗回之後楊堅不再指望一次會戰定江南，而是先修運河、開永濟渠、造大艦、練水軍、儲糧秣，把五年時間花在做準備上。第二步是開皇八年十月下詔之後的分進合擊：楊廣領主力自廣陵出，楊素自永安順流破三峽，王誼自襄漢南下，楊俊在側翼策應，東路奇襲與西路強攻同時壓上，陳朝無法判斷哪一路是主攻。東路靠的是奇襲：賀若弼在廣陵暗中造商船六十餘艘，每船藏五六十人，白天載貨、夜裡換人，順流漂到采石；韓擒虎以五百精兵為後援，取的是人少、夜靜、敵軍酣睡三個條件。登岸之後先取京口，再沿北岸往西壓到白土岡，陳將蕭摩訶的精兵在此崩潰，陳的江防門戶洞開。西方則是水戰：楊素的舟師在峽中遇陳援軍，陳人投火炬，隋兵以帷幕遮蔽、灑水防護，冒矢石突陣，砍斷陳軍的連鎖，舟船相接成浮橋濟渡兵糧，陳軍的舟楫在火中盡毀。合流之後是攻城：賀若弼自西南雨花台逼近城牆，韓擒虎自北面新林登岸，隋軍用覆布車抵近城下，弩手封住射孔，陳軍在城頭以堞與盾抵禦矢石，陳帝與張麗華、孔貴嬪退入景陽殿，藏入枯井，隋軍索繩引出，陳朝至此而亡。整套打法與羅馬的做法形成對照：羅馬攻城靠龜甲陣護住撞槌硬推，隋軍卻寧可奇襲奪灘頭、繞開正面城牆，盾牌的用法是遮蔽與結陣，而不是咬合成牆。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war can be put in one sentence: turn the war into a piece of engineering, and then use the engineering to buy a decision. The first step was the defeat of Kaihuang 7. When the Sui army first crossed the Yangtze, Xiao Mohe burned the ships with fire in the gorges and seven or eight soldiers in ten were killed; after that withdrawal Yang Jian no longer expected a single battle to settle Jiangnan, but first worked on the canals, cut the Yongji channel, built great ships, trained river troops and stored grain, spending five years on the preparation. The second step was the pincer after the edict of the tenth month of Kaihuang 8: Yang Guang took the main force out from Guangling, Yang Su came down from Yong'an with the current and forced the three gorges, Wang Yi descended from the Xiang and Han and Yang Jun operated on the flank, so that a surprise in the east and a forcing in the west came on at once and the Chen could not tell which was the main effort. The eastern line rested on surprise: He Ruobi had sixty-odd merchant ships built in secret at Guangling, each holding fifty or sixty men, carrying cargo by day and taking soldiers by night, and they drifted down to Caishi; Han Qinhu brought up five hundred picked men in support, taking advantage of three things, few men, a quiet night and an enemy asleep. Once ashore, they took Jingkou first and then pressed westward along the north bank to White Mound Hill, where the picked troops of Xiao Mohe collapsed and the river defence of the Chen stood open. The western line was a battle of boats: Yang Su's fleet met a Chen relief force in the gorges, the Chen threw torches, the Sui covered themselves with screens and doused the fire, charged forward under arrows and stones, cut the Chen lashings apart, and lashed their own ships into a floating bridge to carry troops and grain across, while the Chen boats burned. After the lines joined came the siege: He Ruobi came up against the wall from the south-west at Yuhuatai, Han Qinhu landed and attacked from the north at Xinlin, the Sui brought the cloth-covered vehicles up to the foot of the wall, the crossbowmen closed the firing slits, the Chen on the ramparts met the arrows and stones with parapets and shields, and the emperor with Zhang Lihua and the Lady Kong withdrew into the Hall of the Rising Sun and hid in a dry well, from which the Sui drew them out on a rope; there Chen perished. The whole method stands in contrast with the Roman one: the Romans sieged by closing the testudo over the ram and pushing ahead, while the Sui preferred to seize a beachhead by surprise and go around the face of the wall, and the shield was used to cover and to close ranks, not to be locked edge to edge into a wall.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類。年表最確定：開皇元年（581）十一月隋文帝受周恭帝禪，開皇三年（583）十月白道之役大破南犯的突厥，開皇四年（584）開永濟渠，開皇七年（587）六月第一次伐陳兵敗洞口，開皇八年（588）十月下詔伐陳，開皇九年（589）正月韓擒虎、賀若弼渡江、建康陷落，二月陳亡，五月湘州刺史蕭岩以州降隋，陳將王琳據江表反隋，直到開皇十一年（591）才被平定。兵員方面，《資治通鑑》記楊素一路領眾五十一萬，其中包含隨軍丁役與漕運人夫，實際作戰兵力遠少於此；全軍造舟艦二千餘艘，楊素一路有兵船千餘艘、甲士十餘萬；先鋒渡江的兵力不過數千，韓擒虎所部為五百精兵，賀若弼的六十餘艘商船每船藏五六十人。糧秣方面，諸軍各給六十日口糧，舟師另備百日之糧，開皇八年大修江南河渠之後，汴水之粟可以順流抵達江表。距離上，廣陵至建康江程約二百五十公里，采石至京口約一百公里，永安至建康舟行數千里，白道峽長十八里。器械方面，五牙大艦高十餘丈、設樓觀三層、可容數百人，蹶張弩射程約二百步；羅馬方陣盾高約一百零五公分、寬約八十公分、重約六七公斤，最後這一組數字屬於另一個技術傳統，只作對照，不在此役的裝備表內。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several kinds. The chronology is the most certain: in the eleventh month of Kaihuang 1, 581 AD, the Sui emperor took the abdication of the Zhou child-emperor; in the tenth month of Kaihuang 3, 583, the battle of White Way broke the Turks who had come south; in Kaihuang 4, 584, the Yongji canal was cut; in the sixth month of Kaihuang 7, 587, the first campaign against Chen was beaten at Dongkou; in the tenth month of Kaihuang 8, 588, the edict for the campaign against Chen went out; in the first month of Kaihuang 9, 589, Han Qinhu and He Ruobi crossed the river and Jiankang fell, and in the second month the Chen perished; in the fifth month the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Xiao Yan, surrendered his prefecture to the Sui, and the Chen general Wang Lin rose in the far south against the Sui and was not put down until Kaihuang 11, 591. On the strength of men, the Comprehensive Mirror records Yang Su leading five hundred and ten thousand, a figure that includes the servants of the army and the boatmen of the transport, so that the actual fighting force was far smaller; the whole army built more than two thousand warships, and on Yang Su's line alone there were a thousand odd war boats with more than a hundred thousand armoured men; the force that crossed first numbered only a few thousand, Han Qinhu's command being five hundred picked men and He Ruobi's sixty-odd merchant ships holding fifty or sixty men each. On provisions, each army was given sixty days' rations and the river fleet carried a hundred days besides; after the Jiangnan channels were worked on again in Kaihuang 8, the grain of the Bian water could drift down to the far bank of the Yangtze. On distances, the water road from Guangling to Jiankang is about two hundred and fifty kilometres, that from Caishi to Jingkou about a hundred, the boat passage from Yong'an to Jiankang several hundred kilometres by water, and the White Way gorge eighteen li long. On the equipment, the great five-toothed ship was more than ten zhang high, with galleries of three storeys and room for several hundred men, and the drawn crossbow was effective to about two hundred paces; the Roman scutum was about one hundred and five centimetres high, eighty wide and six to seven kilograms in weight, and this last set of figures belongs to a different technological tradition, offered here for comparison only and not on the equipment list of this campaign.
cause: 打起來的原因有四層。最外一層是版圖：北周末年的天下分為北周與南陳，跨越三百年的南北分立只有靠一場戰爭才能了結，楊堅把「混一江南」當作既定方針，這不是臨時起意的念頭，而是他從開皇初年就在籌備的目標。第二層是北方的整合：北周留下的割據勢力與兵權分散，楊堅在建隋前後平掉尉遲迥、王謙與江南高智慧，收宿衛、整府兵，把關隴集團的資源集中到國家手裡，北方越穩，南面的勝算越大。第三層是陳朝自身的崩壞：陳帝寵信張麗華、孔貴嬪，怠於政事，捐國帑修造景陽殿，江南士族多有怨望；將領之間互不信任，裴忌新敗即奔，侯安都甚至叛降隋朝，樞密院與州郡之間的調度屢屢失靈。第四層是隋的國力與戰略前提：開皇年間的休養使府庫充盈、糧食充足，運河把江北剩餘一路運到江表，徵發的工匠與丁役足以支撐一支水陸並行的龐大軍團；開皇七年的敗績把戰爭從會戰改成了工程，開皇八年隋以三十萬眾攻高句麗，掐斷了陳朝可能得到的北方援助。水文與季節也被算進去：冬季水勢順流，楊素的舟師可以一路漂下來，不必再冒在峽中被燒的風險。
causeEn: There were four layers of cause behind the fighting. The outermost was the map: at the end of Northern Zhou the realm was divided between Northern Zhou and the southern Chen, and a division of north and south that had lasted three hundred years could only be ended by a war. Yang Jian treated the uniting of the south as settled policy; this was not an idea that occurred to him on the spur of the moment but a target he had been preparing towards since the early years of Kaihuang. The second layer was the integration of the north: the fragmentary powers and the scattered military authority left over from Northern Zhou meant that Yang Jian, in the years around the foundation of the Sui, put down Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian and the rising of Gao Zhihui in Jiangnan, drew the guards into his own hand, reformed the fubing, and concentrated the resources of the Guanzhong-Longxi group in the state; the steadier the north, the better the odds in the south. The third layer was the collapse inside the Chen itself: the emperor favoured Zhang Lihua and the Lady Kong, neglected business, and spent the resources of the state on the Hall of the Rising Sun, and the great families of the south had much reason for resentment. The commanders did not trust one another; Pei Ji broke and ran as soon as he was defeated, and Hou Andu even defected to the Sui, and the coordination between the Directorate of Military Affairs and the commanderies failed again and again. The fourth layer was the strength of the Sui state and the tactical premises of the campaign: the rest in the Kaihuang years filled the treasuries and the granaries, the canals carried the surplus of the north bank as far as the far shore, and the conscripted craftsmen and labourers could support an enormous army moving by land and by water together. The defeat of Kaihuang 7 turned the war from a battle into a work of engineering; in Kaihuang 8 the Sui sent three hundred thousand men against Goguryeo, which cut off any northern help the Chen might have had. The hydrology and the season were also reckoned with: in winter the water ran downstream, so Yang Su's fleet could drift the whole way without running the risk of being burned in the gorges.
impact: 這場戰爭最深的一層後果落在地圖上。開皇九年二月陳朝覆亡，自東晉十六國以來近三百年的南北分立告一段落，隋成為中國第二個大一統王朝，疆域東至東海、西抵西域、南盡嶺南、北盡大漠，規模在當時前所未有。制度層面上，隋朝在陳的廢墟上建立起延續三百年的帝國框架：三省制的定型、尚書省六部的職掌劃分、州縣兩級的行政、對邊疆的羈縻與都護府體制，都在此後由隋入唐而成型；開皇年間的取士之法——開皇七年詔令諸州舉秀才，其後又下詔令五品以上官員以志行修偉為秀才——被後世視為科舉制度的開端，門閥壟斷官位的局面自此被撬開，江南舊族與北方新貴同場競逐，這是陳亡之後才出現的政治局面；律令方面，開皇二年頒行的新律與開皇年間統一度量衡的詔令，把一個新王朝的規範強加在南北兩套舊制度之上。江南社會本身也經歷震盪：陳朝的大族失去政權與軍權，陳亡之後大批陳人北遷，隋朝一面罷除陳末的苛捐雜賦、合併州縣、重新編定戶籍，一面又在江表屢遭反抗，王琳之外，尚有江南豪族趁亂起事，直到隋末唐初才匯入亂局。物質層面最巨大的工程是運河：永濟渠與江南河渠把南北漕運連成一體，而此役消耗的江南財力與兵源，恰恰是楊廣日後三征高句麗時動用的東西；隋朝在統一之後僅存二十九年就為大亂所覆，隨之而來的唐朝則在隋的制度骨架上重建秩序。於是這場戰爭既是終結，也是開端。
impactEn: The deepest consequence of this war fell on the map. When the Chen perished in the second month of Kaihuang 9, the division of north and south that had lasted close on three hundred years since the Eastern Jin and the Sixteen Kingdoms came to an end, and the Sui became the second unified dynasty in Chinese history, ruling from the eastern sea to the western marches, from Lingnan in the south to the great deserts in the north, over a territory without precedent in the age. At the level of institutions, the Sui built on the ruins of Chen the framework of an empire that would last three hundred years: the fixing of the three departments, the division of functions among the six ministries of the Department of State Affairs, the two-tier administration of commandery and county, and the frontier system of indirect rule and protectorates all took their shape as the Sui handed them to the Tang. The method of selecting officials in the Kaihuang years, the edict of Kaihuang 7 ordering the commanderies to recommend xiucai and the later edict ordering officials of the fifth rank and above to recommend men of notable character, is regarded by later ages as the opening of the examination system, and the monopoly of office by the great families was levered open; old southern clans and new northern men competed on the same ground, and that political situation only became possible after the fall of Chen. In the matter of law and standards, the new statutes promulgated in Kaihuang 2 and the Kaihuang edicts that unified the system of weights and measures imposed the norms of a new dynasty upon two old systems, one from the north and one from the south. Jiangnan society itself was shaken: the great families of the Chen lost both the government and the army, large numbers of Chen people moved north after the fall, and the Sui on the one hand abolished the harsh levies and miscellaneous exactions of late Chen, merged commanderies and counties and compiled the registers of households afresh, and on the other hand was met in the far south by resistance again and again, with the rising of Wang Lin and of other great families of Jiangnan feeding into the disorder of the last years of the Sui and the first of the Tang. On the material side the greatest work was the canal: the Yongji channel and the Jiangnan waterways tied the northern and southern grain routes into one, and the wealth and the manpower of the south consumed by this campaign were precisely what Yang Guang would later spend on three campaigns against Goguryeo; the Sui survived only twenty-nine years after the unification before great disorder swept over it, and the Tang that followed rebuilt order on the Sui's institutional frame. This war was therefore both an end and a beginning.
result: 打完的結局是清楚的：開皇九年（589）二月，隋軍攻入建康，陳帝叔寶與張麗華、孔貴嬪自景陽殿枯井中被擒，陳朝至此而亡，陳的州郡、府庫、版籍盡歸隋室。隋文帝隨後詔封陳帝為懷王，待遇頗為優厚，陳降軍收編入隋軍編制，州郡官吏多仍舊任，而江南則立刻進入收拾與安撫並行的狀態：罷除苛捐、合併州縣、重新括籍、遣官鎮撫。但過程並不乾淨：陳將王琳乘虛據江表起兵反隋，開皇九年五月湘州刺史蕭岩以州降隋，開皇十一年王琳才被平定，江南全部歸附因此拖了近三年；同一時期江南豪族的小規模起事此伏彼起，說明軍事上的統一完成得快，而秩序上的統一遠沒有那麼快。就戰役本身的技術層面，隋朝的取勝可歸納為四點：以開皇七年的敗績為鑑，耗五年把舟師與糧秣整備到能順流攻擊的程度；西路楊素的水軍破三峽，東路韓擒虎、賀若弼奇襲渡江，使陳朝無法集中兵力；以北方高句麗戰線牽制陳的外援；再以一場夜渡和不足兩月的推進，壓垮一個尚有數百萬人口的南朝。傳世記載中最著名的一段，是陳帝在隋廷宴席上盛稱江南地廣物豐、稻米支給皆足，隋文帝應以天下方安、須養蒼生之語，一個王朝的末路與另一個王朝的自我期許同時被寫在史冊上；而《玉樹後庭花》被後人譜成亡國之音，讓這場戰爭在記憶裡獲得了一個比任何戰術細節都更長久的形狀。
resultEn: The outcome of the fighting is clear: in the second month of Kaihuang 9, 589 AD, the Sui army entered Jiankang, the emperor Chen Shubao together with Zhang Lihua and the Lady Kong were taken from the dry well of the Hall of the Rising Sun, the Chen perished there, and the commanderies, the treasuries and the registers of the Chen passed entire into the Sui house. The Sui emperor then enfeoffed the fallen emperor as Prince of Huai and treated him with a good deal of care; the surrendered troops of the Chen were taken into the Sui order of battle, the commandery and county officials of the Chen were largely left in their posts, and Jiangnan at once entered a period in which tidying up and pacification went on together: the harsh levies were abolished, commanderies and counties were merged, the registers of households were compiled afresh and officials were sent to hold the peace. But the process was not clean. The Chen general Wang Lin rose against the Sui and occupied the far south on the strength of the moment; in the fifth month of Kaihuang 9 the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Xiao Yan, surrendered his prefecture; Wang Lin was not put down until Kaihuang 11, and the complete submission of Jiangnan was therefore delayed by nearly three years. Small risings by the great families of Jiangnan followed one another in the same period, which shows that the unification was achieved quickly in military terms and far more slowly in terms of order. As to the technical side of the campaign itself, the Sui victory can be reduced to four things: taking the defeat of Kaihuang 7 as its lesson and spending five years bringing the river fleet and the grain up to a standard that allowed an attack with the current; using the water army of Yang Su in the west to force the gorges together with the surprise crossing of Han Qinhu and He Ruobi in the east, so that the Chen could not concentrate its forces; holding down the northern approach with the Goguryeo front; and then bringing down a southern state of several million people with one night crossing and less than two months of advance. The most famous passage in the received record is that of the fallen emperor praising, at a banquet of the Sui court, the breadth and richness of the south and how ample were its rice rations, and the Sui emperor answering that the realm had only just been brought to peace and that the people must be given a living, so that the end of one dynasty and the self-expectation of another were written into the annals at once; and the Yu Shu Hou Ting Hua was later set to music as the song of a lost state, which gave this war in memory a shape longer-lasting than any tactical detail.
